matches.differs: K-629 / K-628 are real fold-up mini-books (one sheet folded twice): a front cover with the title (K-628 adds an illustrator line) and three pages with one sentence each. They have no title page, no back cover, no page numbers and no tasks (circle the title, star the back cover, number the pages, match cover/title/page). Far: a print-concepts mode of types/_shared/reader-book.js with an 8-page fold, title page, back cover and the three task levels.

The mini-books practise tracking in a real book: K-629 'point under each word as you read', page by page; K-628 pages break over 2-3 lines ("Kit the cat | sat on a mat."), so the return sweep happens. No page prints start/stop dots or left-to-right and return-sweep arrows to trace or draw, and none asks to number the words. New layout (print-concepts page), not a small change.

K-552 Sentence Strips prints 2-4 picture sentences as one word card per word that the child cuts apart and rebuilds (one card = one word), and K-629 has the child point under each word; neither has the row of empty boxes to colour one per spoken word, nor the 3-word / 4-5-word sentence ladder. Small change: a box row under each K-552 sentence.

K-552 makes the word boundaries physical (cut the sentence into word cards); K-527 Trace a Sentence has the child copy a sentence (finger spaces). Nothing asks to draw a line in each space, count the words and write the number. Small change: a count-the-words mode over the K-552/K-527 sentence bank.

G1-314 Blend the Sounds prints the word's sounds in boxes (L1 3-4 sounds) and the child blends them and circles the matching picture of three. It is phoneme-by-phoneme blending from PRINTED letters, not oral onset-rime blending the teacher says (/s/ ... /un/), and it has no levels by distractor kind (different first sound / same first sound / same rime). Moderate change: an oral 'teacher says it' mode with no letters and rime-controlled picture triples.
7 English picture readers (I See Pets, At the Farm, My Lunch ...): cover + three pages of one patterned sentence each; K-630 is the same book to colour, K-631 the Read and Talk companion page.
K-230 sorts letters into vowels and consonants; K-533 colours every vowel in picture words (L1 four 3-5-letter words), the second half of the objective.

K-227 Middle Sounds: CVC pictures, the child writes the middle vowel; K-224: write the missing (vowel) letter. Both mix all five vowels on every page and cannot be limited to short a / short i; the K-227 bank holds 18 words (a 6, i 3, o 4, u 3, e 2), too few for twelve words of one vowel. No read-the-word-and-match half, no two-column sort. G1-306 has -an and -at families (onset writing). Small-to-moderate change: a vowel unit axis + a larger CVC bank.

Same as en-K-008: the medial-vowel pages mix all vowels and the bank is thin (o 4, u 3, e 2 words in K-227); no one-vowel page, no read-and-match half, no two-column sort. Needs a vowel unit axis and a larger CVC bank.

No word-chain / word-ladder page exists. Build a 'chain' mode of types/_shared/lit-word-build.js (the K-224/K-231 factory): a bank of CVC chains where each step changes one letter (first, last, then middle), with pictures.

G1-330 Word Families: Read and Circle shows a picture and a column of words from the same rime row (can / fan / pan / van) and the child circles the one that names it: real words differing in the FIRST letter only (the need's level 1). Nothing pairs words differing in the last letter or the middle vowel (cat/cot, pin/pen), and nothing asks to underline the letter that differs. G1-552 compares a word with misspellings (non-words). Small change: a minimal-pair bank with first/last/middle levels.

5 English decodable mini-books (Dad and Sam, Kit and the Dog ...), every word gated to the taught sounds and heart words, no pictures: the child reads each page and draws it; K-631 is the companion page.

G1-506 Story Map is the organiser (L1 boxes Beginning 'Who is in the story? Where are they?', Middle 'What happens?', End, each with a draw box and 2 lines) for any read-aloud, but it prints no story and has no picture choices. G2-254's stories (30-73 words, narratives) ask who/where among 3 word-choice questions, not pictures. Moderate: a read-aloud picture-panel story bank + Who/Where/What-happened boxes.

K-381 is the need's level 1 (cut out three pictures, glue them in First / Next / Last; L1 one strip), G1-401 the level-2 drawing (draw the middle between the given beginning and end). But the strips are wordless object-change sequences (an apple eaten, a fence painted), not a story with characters read aloud, and there is no retell frame (First ___. Then ___.). Moderate: a read-aloud story bank on the same layouts.

G2-254 has stories the teacher can read (L2 published pool 44-73 words) with 3 key-detail questions (who, what, where, why, how does X feel) but the answers are three printed WORDS/phrases, which a kindergartner cannot read; no picture answers and no own-question box. Moderate: picture-answer questions for a short read-aloud story.

Level 1 (one story of four sentences): the child numbers the sentences and draws a line from each to its picture. The 'stories' are four-step picture sequences (an apple eaten bite by bite, a fence being painted), not a tale with characters; the teacher reads the sentences.

No page compares two stories. Build a paired-story bank (two short read-aloud stories with panels) on the two-card compare layout of G2-342 (compare mode of G2-318) or a Venn cut-and-paste like K-240.

G1-293 Nouns and Verbs: Two Bins, level 1: 3 nouns + 3 verbs, the nouns with a small picture, the child copies each word into the naming or the doing bin. The verbs have no picture (a kindergartner cannot read them), the child writes rather than cuts and pastes, and there is no 'The ___ can ___.' frame. Small change: action pictures (library 'activities' theme) and a cut-and-sort mode.

Maths-catalogue type (K.G.A.1, Position Words maker). K-548 level 1: in, on top of, under, next to; level 3 adds behind and in front of (circle the word that fits the sentence for each scene). The relation is a picture and a shape, not a cat and a box. K-546 (published) is the need's level 3: read the sentence and draw the picture in place.

G1-498 prints sentences in small letters only and the child circles every word that needs a capital: the first word, the word I and names (L1 four sentences, L3 rewrite). Sentences are 5-8 words (not 3), names are mixed in, and no page prints mostly correct sentences with a few small-letter starts to fix. Small change: a K level with 3-4-word sentences and no names.

G2-282 level 1: broken sentences (no capital, no end mark, one name) that the child rewrites with a capital and the right end mark, . or ?. It asks a K child to rewrite whole sentences, has no pictures and no half-telling/half-asking structure for writing only the mark. Small change: a 'write only the end mark' K level with pictures.

G1-503 Stretch the Sentence: a short sentence (The big dog plays.), the questions Where? When? (How? from L2) with a line each, then the longer sentence. Same skill (expand with where/when/how) but no picture, no box of add-ons to circle or copy; the child must invent and write the phrases (G1 demand). Small change: a K level with a picture and a printed add-on box.
No multiple-meaning (homograph) page exists. Build a two-picture homograph bank (bat, duck, ring, bark, top, can) as a mode of the word-picture matcher types/_shared/lit-vocab-match.js (K-225).

There is no information-text-with-questions page. The nearest is G2-343 Who Am I? Mystery Animal: three cards of five first-person fact clues and a bank of six animal pictures (answer = the animal: a picture choice). It answers 'who am I', not who/what/where/how questions about a 30-word fact text, and is G2 reading. Far: an information-text bank (30-80 words per grade) with picture-answer questions.

G2-488 Which Title Fits?: two passages without titles, circle the title that fits of three: the main-topic idea. The passages are narrative stories (30-73 words), not information texts, the answers are printed titles (no pictures), and there are no key-detail boxes. Needs an information-text bank.

Science-catalogue types. G2-364 Parts of a Plant and Their Functions: five job phrases (root 'takes in water from the soil', stem, leaf, flower, seed) matched to numbered tags on a plant picture by writing the tag number: the text-to-picture link the lesson teaches. One level only (five parts), phrases not a four-sentence text, numbered tags instead of word labels; G1-376 labels the parts from a word bank (the level-3 'add a label'). Small change: a 2-/4-label K ladder and a line-drawing answer.

Science-catalogue types. G1-203 The Life Cycle of a Chicken: number three pictures 1-2-3 (egg to chick, the need's own example); G1-377 the butterfly. There is no information text to read and no 'First ___, then ___' frame; it sequences pictures rather than connecting two ideas in a text. Small change for the picture part; the text needs an information-text bank.

G2-342 Compare Two Animals: two printed animal fact files (class, habitat, diet, covering), circle same or different per fact, then write two same and two different: a G2 reading/writing load with no running text and no picture cards. G3-393 (science) checks butterfly / frog / both per sentence. Far: two read-aloud texts on one topic + a picture-card Venn sort.

K-554 My Reading Log names the book (title, author), rates it with stars, asks 'My favorite part' and a drawing; K-342 has the child circle a favourite picture and copy its word. Neither has the opinion frames 'My favorite ___ is ___. I like it because ___.', a word bank or the 3-icon checklist. Small change: an opinion frame with the writing-frames.js starter blanks.

G1-509 Describe the Character: a big picture and the starters My character's name is ___ / is ___ and ___ / likes ___ / lives in ___ with a word bank (L1-2): describing a pictured animal, not the child's own topic, and no labelled drawing box. K-555 gives a picture and one line; G2-318 a fact file of one animal. None prints This is a ___. It has ___. It can ___., a box for a labelled drawing or the checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

G1-506 Story Map L1: beginning / middle / end boxes with a draw box and 2 lines each, prompts about a story (Who is in the story?), not a personal small moment. Missing the two picture boxes First/Then, the frames First I ___. Then I ___. I felt ___., the word bank and the checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

K-326 Beginning, Middle or End: the child colours the box where the week's letter sound is heard; level 1 = beginning or end only (3-0-3), level 3 = four middle cards: the need's ladder. But the pictures are words of any length (mailbox) and 'middle' is a consonant inside a long word, not the vowel of a CVC/CCVC word; K-227 covers the medial vowel separately. Small change: a one-syllable picture filter and vowel units.

Of the three spellings only ck exists: the G2-315 rule 'c, k or ck' (G2-324 Which One?, G2-326 sort) has ck words (sock, lock, duck, rocket) mixed with c/k choices. No ng and no wh unit in any type (G1-311 Sound of the Week has sh, ch, th only). Small change: ng and wh units in data/b3/spelling-rules.js or the letter-of-the-week bank.

Initial blends (bl br cl cr dr fl fr gl gr pl pr sk sl sm sn sp st sw tr tw; 57 pictures): L1 circle the blend of three, L2 write the two letters before the printed rest (__og), L3 from the picture. A page spreads over all blends (no s-blends-only level 1), about a third of the words have two or more syllables (bracelet, broccoli, dragonfly), and there is no read-and-match half. G1-333 adds blend word-family ladders.

No final-blend bank exists. G1-306 has one final-blend family, -and (hand, sand), among CVC rimes; G1-493 does INITIAL blends only. Small change: a final-blend bank (nd, mp, st, nk) for the G1-493 factory.

Level 1: a 43-73-word story with numbered sentences and 3 literal questions (who, what, where, when, why), each with a 'Sentence N' chip that sends the child to the sentence holding the answer. 3 multiple-choice questions, not 4; the stories are not strictly decodable (pumpkins, librarian); the child is shown the sentence rather than underlining it. G1-504 asks the same passages as open questions on lines (3/4/5 questions).

G1-506 is a story map but its boxes are beginning / middle / end (L3 + problem), not characters / setting / big events, and it prints no story; G2-254 prints stories (43-73 words) whose questions touch who and where but carry no story map. Small change: a characters-setting-events box set in G1-506 + a story from the G2-254 pools.

Retelling exists: G2-378 Retell with Starters (one 4-picture sequence, write each picture starting First / Next / Then / Finally; L1 one line each) and the G1-506 story map. No fable bank and no lesson / central-message line anywhere (G2-488 picks a title, not a lesson). Far: a fable bank with lesson choices.

K-319 Feelings matches six faces to feeling words (part of level 1); G2-254 asks 'How does X feel?' about its stories. No page has the child underline feeling and sense words in a story or poem, and no sense words appear. Moderate: a short story/poem bank with tagged feeling and sense words.
No page asks who is speaking (narrator or character). Build a dialogue-story bank with speaker tags; the speech-bubble frames of G1-507 (writing-frames.js bubble) could carry level 1.

G2-315 unit 'Magic e' (a_e i_e o_e u_e; 48 picture words, L1 3-8 letters): read the rule box, write the vowel and the final e into the gaps. Mostly long words (lemonade, telephone, porcupine), no cap/cape pairs, no 'add an e and read the new word' task, no a_e-only level. Small change: CVC/CVCe pair bank + a vowel-by-vowel level.

Level 1 (six one-syllable words): the child says each word and circles the long line or the short dot. The word is printed with its vowel coloured (the spelling shows the length) and all vowels mix; there is no cut-and-sort into two boxes and no one-vowel level.

The G2-315 rule 'ai or ay' exists (fill the gap; G2-326 sorts picture words into an ai bin and an ay bin; G2-324 circles ai or ay) but its 21 words hold only 2 ay words (playground, haystack), too few for the sort faces, most are two-syllable (raincoat, sailboat, waitress), and 6 are not long a at all (chair, armchair, hair, stairs, eclair, wheelchair: /air/). Small change: a corrected long-a bank with one-syllable ai and ay words.

The G2-315 rule 'ee or ea' exists (40 words; G2-326 sort into ee / ea bins) but mixes words where the letters do not spell long e: ear, earmuffs, deer, reindeer, meerkat (r-controlled) and cereal, theater (e and a in two syllables); most words are two-syllable. Small change: clean the bank to one-syllable long-e words.

The spelling-rules factory has no oa/ow unit (en units: magic-e, c-k-ck, ee-ea, ai-ay, floss, y-ies-f-ves). Small change: an oa-ow rule unit in data/b3/spelling-rules.js; the pages (gap, sort, which one) exist.

G1-498 Capital Letters: sentences in small letters, circle each word needing a capital (first word, names, I; L3 rewrite). Its 18 sentences hold names only; the generator states that weekdays and months are not in them. No date or own-name writing. Small change: sentences with days and months.

No conjunction page exists. Build a join-two-sentences mode over the tagged sentence bank (data/grammar/grammar-tables.js, types/_shared/sentence-items.js, the G1-502 Sentence Halves factory) with an and/but/so/because box.

G2-317 Verb Forms (en 'today and yesterday'): a table of six pictured verbs with the columns 'he/she today' and 'yesterday' + three sentence gaps; the bank mixes 14 regular (jumped, hopped, carried) and 14 irregular verbs. No 'tomorrow / will' column and no regular-only level. Small change: a future column + a regular -ed level.

G1-506 Story Map plans a story (beginning / middle / end boxes with prompts, draw box + 2-3 lines); G2-378 writes a picture sequence with First / Next / Then / Finally starters. No true-story planner with first/next/last + a 6-line draft page, no time-word frames on every line, no checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

No opinion-writing page exists. Build an opinion frame (opinion box, reason box, I think ___. One reason is ___. That is why ___., checklist) with the starter/line/box pieces of types/_shared/writing-frames.js (G1-506 / G1-509 family).

G2-341 Fact File: Write Three Sentences: a printed animal fact file, finish three sentences with its facts, then one fact of the child's own. The topic is always a given animal, there is no topic sentence frame, no closing sentence and no checklist; G2-318 is the empty fact file to research. Small change: an informative frame (This is all about ___ ... Now you know ___).

G2-274 Fix the Sentence covers the edit half: broken sentences (no capital, no end mark, lowercase names) rewritten on lines, with a checklist banner (A · Aa · .?!). There is no sample piece with mixed mistakes, no revise check (add a detail, heart words), and no checklist for the child's own draft. Small change: a checklist page in writing-frames.js.

Category sorts exist (K-240 cut, sort and paste into 2-3 bins; K-511 sort by a rule; K-550 name the group), but on broad categories (animals, fruits, vehicles, clothes), not birds / fish / bugs, and nothing asks for a definition 'A ___ is a ___ that ___'. Small change: sub-category bins + a definition-frame row.

G2-317 writes a verb's -s form ('he/she today') and its past (regular -ed and irregular mixed) in a table; G2-337 circles the fitting form of three under a sentence. No -ing column anywhere, irregular pasts mix in, and no 'circle the base word'. Small change: an -s/-ed/-ing column set with regular verbs only.

G1-504 Read and Answer has the right shape (a passage, 3/4/5 key-detail questions with answer lines) but its passages are narrative stories (30-73 words), not information texts with a heading and a picture; G2-343 reads animal fact clues. Moderate: an information-text bank (about 70 words) for the G1-504/G2-254 pages; the question formats exist.
G2-488 Which Title Fits?: two untitled passages, circle the title of three (main topic). Narrative stories, not information texts; no key-detail boxes. Needs an information-text bank.
No text-features page exists (no text with headings, bold words, captions or a glossary anywhere in the banks). Build an information-text bank with marked features and a find-it question page.

The ready material of the grade-2 point (en-2-078) serves here too: two printed animal fact files (class, habitat, diet, covering), circle same or different for each fact, then write two things that are the same and two that are different. The 'texts' are fact-file tables, not 40-word running texts, and there is no fact-strip sort level.

G1-329 Vowel King is exactly this (every syllable has one vowel: dot the vowel in each printed syllable arc) but it is REFUSED for English by design (bank kings:false; published in de and sv only). G1-305 counts syllables by clapping and drawing arcs, not by vowels. Small change: enable English with a closed-syllable word filter (napkin, basket).

G2-330 Split the Compound (draw a line where the second word starts; L1 shows the parts) = level 1; G1-324 Syllable Cards (read the word one syllable at a time, L1 two syllables) = level 2 (rabbit, picnic); G2-332 Compound Detective (12 words, circle the 6 compounds and write their parts) = level 3. Three pages, not one; no picture of each small word.

Sight-word pages exist (K-437 missing letters, K-433 read-trace-write + sentences, K-390 one sentence step by step); said and was are in the English word list, of, could and would are not. No sound boxes with a heart over the tricky part. Small change: add the words + a heart-word mapping mode in types/_shared/sight-word-pages.js.

Level 2 (eight one-syllable words) or level 3 (two-syllable words too): say the word, circle the long line or the short dot; long = silent e or ai ay ee oa igh ie. Marking, not sorting into two columns; no hop/hope sentence choice.

Two of the three pairs exist as G2-315 rule units (ai or ay, ee or ea; G2-326 sorts into two bins) but oa/ow does not, the ai-ay bank has only 2 ay words and 6 /air/ words (chair, hair, stairs ...), and the ee-ea bank holds r-controlled and split-vowel words (ear, deer, reindeer, cereal, theater). No all-six-teams page. Small change: an oa-ow unit + cleaned long-a / long-e banks.

The spelling-rules factory (gap, sort, which-one pages) has no oo, ou/ow or oi/oy unit in English. Small change: three rule units in data/b3/spelling-rules.js (with the oi-middle / oy-end and ou-middle / ow-end rule).

G2-254 level 3: 2 inference questions + 1 written answer about stories with a small problem (a tower washed away, a stuck ball) and 'How does X feel?' questions. Stories are 58-73 words (not ~150), there is no challenge / what-the-character-did / feeling organizer and no quote-as-proof. Moderate: longer stories + an organizer layout.

Retelling exists (G2-378: write a 4-picture sequence with First / Next / Then / Finally), the moral does not: no fable or folktale in any bank and no lesson line (G2-488 chooses a title). Far: a fable bank (~150 words) with retell strips and lesson choices.

G1-506 Story Map L3 (beginning / problem / middle / end, draw box + 2 lines each) plans a story; G2-378 drafts a picture sequence with time-word starters. No who-and-where / feelings planner for a personal small moment, no 10-line draft page, no checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

Only the editing part exists: G2-282 / G2-274 rewrite broken single sentences (capital, names, end mark) with a checklist banner. No sample story with mixed mistakes, no revise checks (detail, stronger word, word-wall spelling), no checklist for the own draft.
No ar/or unit in the spelling-rules factory (English units: magic-e, c-k-ck, ee-ea, ai-ay, floss, y-ies-f-ves). Small change: an ar-or rule unit; the gap, sort and which-one pages exist.
No er/ir/ur unit in the spelling-rules factory. Small change: an er-ir-ur rule unit (three bins on the G2-326 sort face).

Two-syllable reading pages exist (G1-325 write the word with a dash at each break, G1-331 join two syllables, G1-324 read the word in parts) but none marks the long vowel or groups words by kind (vowel-team compound / silent e / open first syllable), and the English splits follow dictionary hyphenation (bak-er, bik-ing, hik-ing, skat-ing), which contradicts the open-syllable rule of level 3 (pa-per, mu-sic). Moderate: a decoding-split bank by syllable type.

The sight-word pages exist but none of could, would, should, because, friend is in the English word list (Dolch pre-primer to grade 1), and there is no sound-box + heart mapping. Small change: add the words + a heart-word mode.

G2-488 picks the title that fits a whole passage (main topic) but its passages are one-paragraph narrative stories (30-73 words); no three-paragraph information text, no per-paragraph focus. Needs an information-text bank.
No text with captions, bold words, subheadings, a glossary or an index exists. Build an information-text bank with marked features and a find-it question page.

Science-catalogue types. G2-365 Label the Butterfly Life Cycle: write the four stage names from a bank under their pictures and cross out the name that does not belong; G1-377 numbers the stages. No 120-word text and no questions answered from the diagram or from text + diagram. Moderate: a short text + diagram questions on the G2-365 layout.

G2-378 Retell with Starters writes a 4-step process sequence (making a sandwich, painting a fence, building a snowman) with First / Next / Then / Finally; G1-402 orders the sentences of a sequence. Pictures, not a 150-word how-it-is-made information text, and no 'why must this step come first'. Moderate: process texts on the same layouts.

G2-318 Animal Fact File groups facts by fields (class, habitat, diet, covering, + legs, fly) on one animal with a draw box; G2-381 My Habitat Report. The topic is given (an animal / a habitat), there is no introduction line, no free fact groups and no checklist. Small change: an informative planner in writing-frames.js.
G2-341 turns a printed fact file into three sentences + one own fact. No 12-line draft under group headings, no linking words in the margin, no definition, no closing, no checklist.

G2-318 is the note-taking fact file for a class research topic (W.2.7), but it gives no source texts; G2-342 prints two fact files. No two 80-word texts, no question-led organizer, no report page with heading. Far: two-text research set.

Split over two pages: G2-376 reads the meaning and writes the prefix for re- / pre- / mis- (10 rows; only reread, refill, retell for re-), G2-320 adds un- / dis- / in- to make the opposite (L1 prints the prefix). No un- + re- page with 'not ___ / ___ again' meaning matches and no sentence gaps. Small change: an un-/re- prefix-key set in data/b5/word-parts.js.

G2-359 sorts derived words onto their root's wall: families help, play, care, use, joy, fear, act, sleep with members such as helpful, helpless, careless, playful, sleepily. The suffixes appear but the child sorts by ROOT and never says what -ful / -less / -ly adds; no meaning match, no build-the-word sentences. Small change: a suffix-meaning mode over the same bank.

No contraction or apostrophe-possessive page exists. The owner-and-thing picture layout of G2-354 (Possessive Pronouns, G1-352 factory) could take a possessive-noun mode; contractions need a new word-pair page.

No page links describing words to real things. Build a describing-word bank with draw-or-name boxes; nearest pieces: the adjective bank of G1-509 (data/b3/opposites.js) and the G1-396 shades-of-meaning rows.

No page has adverbs (the word-class banks hold nouns, verbs, adjectives). Build an adjective/adverb pair bank on the G2-337 choose-the-form layout (two forms under a sentence) with an arrow-to-the-word task.

G1-506 Story Map L3 (beginning / problem / middle / end) is the arc organizer; G1-401 draws the middle between a beginning and an end. Neither prints a story (~150 words) or asks what the beginning introduces and how the end solves the problem. Moderate: a story bank with the arc questions.
No dialogue story and no speaker/point-of-view task exists. Build a dialogue-story bank with speaker tags; the G1-507 speech-bubble frame could carry the 'what would each say next' part.
No page compares two versions of a tale. Build a paired-tale bank on the two-card compare layout of G2-342 (rows characters / setting / problem / ending).
No opinion planner exists. Build it in types/_shared/writing-frames.js (opinion box, three reason boxes, closing box, linking words, checklist).
No opinion draft page exists. Build it in writing-frames.js (12 lines under opinion / reasons / closing headings, linking words in the margin, checklist).

G1-510 Write a Postcard, level 3 = a letter on the whole page (8 lines) with 'Dear ___,' and 'Love,' printed. No date line, no labelled parts, the commas are printed (not practised), no sample letter with missing commas, no second reader. Small change: a letter-parts level.

G1-498 is the circle-the-capitals page, but its sentences carry only names, I and the first word; no holidays, places or product names, and no needs-a-capital sort. Small change: a sentence set tagged for holidays / places / brands.

Syllable pages exist (G1-325 write the word with a dash at each break, G1-326 missing syllable) but none names closed or open syllables, and the English splits are dictionary hyphenation (bak-er, bik-ing) and, in the broader pool, closed-first splits for open-syllable words (tig-er, rob-ot, pap-er), so they cannot teach ro-bot / ti-ger. Far: a decoding-split bank by syllable type + a C/O marking mode.

No page names syllable types; consonant-le words (table, puzzle) are not in the English syllable pool at all. Far: a syllable-type bank (silent-e, vowel-team, C-le) and a name-the-type mode on the G1-305 factory.

The word-part families carry the suffixes (helpful, helpless, carelessness, enjoyment, enjoyable, fearlessness) but the child sorts by root (G2-359) or fills sentence gaps (G3-399); no circle base / underline suffix / meaning match, no -ness/-ment-focused level, no base-changes level (happiness). Small change: a suffix mode over data/b5/word-parts.js.
The sight-word pages exist but the English list is Dolch pre-primer to grade 1: none of enough, though, ocean, laugh, through. Small change: grade-3 heart words + a heart-word mode.

G2-254 level 1 numbers the sentences and points each literal question to its sentence (evidence), level 3 adds a written answer. Stories are one paragraph of 58-73 words (need ~250 words in numbered paragraphs), 3 questions, no box for the proving paragraph, no copying the exact words.
